Building Classification Models Using Wines Data¶

This project showcases the supervised machine learning classification models by building and evaluating various models. The dataset for this project is the wines dataset from scikit-learn library. The project entails exploration and visualization of the data, later on training six different models: Logistic Regression,Decision Tree,Random Forest,Support Vector Machine (SVM),k-Nearest Neighbours, and Naive Bayes. In the end, there is model evaluation using the standard evaluation metrics the performance of each model and recommending the best model.

1. Loading the dataset¶

In [1]:
import pandas as pd
              import numpy as np
              import seaborn as sns
              import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
              from sklearn import datasets
In [2]:
# Loading the dataset
              wines = datasets.load_wine()
              df = pd.concat([pd.DataFrame(wines.data, columns=wines.feature_names), pd.DataFrame(wines.target, columns=['class'])], axis=1)
              df['class'] = df['class'].map({0: 'class_0', 1: 'class_1', 2: 'class_2'})

Creating Train and Test Set¶
In [14]:
# Importing the required libraries
            from sklearn.model_selection import  train_test_split
            from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
            X_data = df.drop(columns=['class'])
            y_data = wines.target
            
            x_train, x_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X_data, y_data, test_size=0.2, random_state=9072025) # Used 80%
            
            # Indentify numeric columns
            numeric_columns = df.select_dtypes(include=np.number).columns.to_list()
            # Scaling data (numeric features)
            # Define and initialize the scaler
            scaler = StandardScaler().fit(X_data)
            # Transform the data
            x_train[numeric_columns] = scaler.transform(x_train[numeric_columns])
            x_test[numeric_columns] = scaler.transform(x_test[numeric_columns])
            
            x_train.head()

4. Model Building¶

Loading the Required Libraries

In [16]:
from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, precision_score, recall_score, f1_score, confusion_matrix, ConfusionMatrixDisplay

1. Logistic Regression¶

Training Logistic Model

In [23]:
# Import libraries
            from sklearn.linear_model import  LogisticRegression
            # Define the Model
            lr_model = LogisticRegression(random_state=10072025)
            # Train the Model
            lr_model.fit(x_train, y_train)
            # Make Predictions
            lr_predictions = lr_model.predict(x_test)

Evaluating Logistic Regression Model

In [24]:
# Evaluate thr model
            print(f"Logistic Regression Model Metrics\n{'*'*40}\nAccuracy Score: {round(accuracy_score(y_test, lr_predictions), 4)}")
            print(f"Precision Score: {round(precision_score(y_test, lr_predictions, average='weighted'),4)}")
            print(f"Recall Score: {round(recall_score(y_test, lr_predictions, average='weighted'),4)}")
            print(f"F1 Score: {round(f1_score(y_test, lr_predictions, average='weighted'),4)}")

Comparing the Models¶

In [78]:
# Define a function to compare models
            
            def compare_models(x_data, y_valid):
            data = {'Model': [], 'Accuracy Score': [], 'Precision Score': [], 'Recall Score': [], 'F1 Score': []}
            models = [lr_model, dt_model, rf_model, svm_model, knn_model, nb_model]
            for model in models:
            predictions = model.predict(x_test)
            data['Model'].append(model.__class__.__name__)
            data['Accuracy Score'].append(round(accuracy_score(y_valid, predictions), 4))
            data['Precision Score'].append(round(precision_score(y_valid, predictions, average='weighted'), 4))
            data['Recall Score'].append(round(recall_score(y_valid, predictions, average='weighted'), 4))
            data['F1 Score'].append(round(f1_score(y_valid, predictions, average='weighted'), 4))
            return pd.DataFrame(data).sort_values(by = ['Accuracy Score', 'F1 Score'], ascending = [False, False])
            compare_models(x_test, y_test)

Making New Predictions¶

In [58]:
def make_new_predictions(data, model = rf_model):
            df = data.copy()
            data[numeric_columns] = scaler.transform(data[numeric_columns])
            predictions = model.predict(data)
            return pd.concat([df, pd.DataFrame(predictions, columns=['predicted_class'])], axis=1)
